regime: Overheat: strong growth (Q3 GDP 3.4%), firm labor (payrolls +165k, claims 200k) and sticky inflation (core CPI +0.3% m/m three months running) with the Fed hiking into 2027, a 5% 10Y and the AI trade being de-rated
summary: Since Nov 2 the regime shifted from 'stagflation-lite' to 'overheat': hiring re-accelerated, October core CPI met Waller's 50bp bar, a December hike is fully priced and futures add about two more hikes by mid-2027 with the 10Y at 5.07%. Oil fell from ~$106 to the low $90s on Iran diplomacy, then bounced on Trump's 'we don't need a deal' post, and Nvidia's CEO resigned on Nov 12, deepening the AI de-rating. The portfolio keeps energy, defense, quality health care and defensive consumer, adds JPM to the higher-for-longer financials theme (the rotation data flags financials as favored and turning), drops WMB (Stage 1, below its averages) and resets the watch-list entries to current supports. COST is near its 1100 target; its stop is raised to 1015 to lock in most of the gain.
drivers: Fed funds futures: Dec 9 implied 4.17% (+29bp), about 4.7% by July 2027; core CPI 3-month annualized 3.8%
10Y 5.07%, 10Y real yield 2.66% (98th percentile); equity risk premium negative (SPY -0.92pp, QQQ -1.52pp)
Labor firm: payrolls +165k (3-month average +137k), unemployment 4.1%, claims 200k
Oil: Brent 93.76 after -11.6% in a month; Trump says no Iran deal is needed; OPEC+ Nov 29
AI de-rating: SOXX -20.8% in 30 days; Nvidia CEO resignation Nov 12; reported export-control review
Rotation: financials, materials, health care and staples lead SPY over 1-3 months; RSP/SPY breadth risk-on
risks: An Iran deal after all drops WTI below $80 and reverses the energy theme
The Fed overtightens (50bp in December, 10Y above 5.3%) and hits valuations broadly, including defensives on high P/Es (COST 43.8x, WMT 39.3x)
An AI-led unwind of the 258% market-cap/GDP valuation drags all equities
A sharp bond rally (10Y below 4.6%) favors the growth names the portfolio underweights
Credit: a break of the HY ETF 76.41 low would hit banks and insurers

themes.name: Higher-for-longer financials
themes.why: A Fed hiking into 2027 lifts float income for insurers and net interest income for money-center banks; the rotation model flags financials as favored in overheat and turning now.

themes.name: Defense and geopolitics
themes.why: An unresolved Iran war and depleted munitions stockpiles; Lockheed's backlog is a record and the breakout above 587 holds.

themes.why: Consumer sentiment near record lows and high prices push trade-down to warehouse and discount retail; staples lead SPY over 1 and 3 months.
